diagram_previews.alt: Case 1: isosceles triangle ABC with points P and Q on BC (order B, P, Q, C), blue segments AP and AQ, the dashed altitude AH, tick marks showing BP = QC, and red arcs marking the equal angles BAP and CAQ.

Case 2: the same triangle with the order B, Q, P, C; blue segments AQ and AP, the dashed altitude AH, red arcs marking angles BAP and CAQ, and double arrows below BC showing the equal lengths BP and QC.

difficulty_rationale: Needs the idea of comparing two pairs of equal-area triangles through the sine area formula; the angle relation must be checked for both orders of P and Q.
